Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. As we move toward contract, our SRE team raised a couple of asks around how Redwood handles progressive rollouts and automatic fallback when serving critical patient triage features. Specifically: 

- We need an explicit canary/autorevert policy documented that we can reference in the contract (what triggers an automatic fallback, metrics and thresholds).
- We need the ability to pin a stable model version for a percent of traffic (or a route) as an emergency escape hatch.
- Telemetry: we need audit logs and per-request latency/error traces for 90 days for compliance.

Can you share a recommended policy and confirm whether automatic fallback + pinning is acceptable as an SLA mitigation (so we can avoid overly strict uptime credits)? Also, procurement will want sample contract language.

Appreciate it — we’re trying to align procurement and engineering timelines.

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya and Laura to keep procurement and the commercial timeline aligned.

High level: yes, we can support an automatic canary fallback and version pinning as part of an SLA mitigation strategy. We typically combine three levers:

- Canary gating: progressive traffic ramp (0 -> X%) with telemetry gates (p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate) evaluated at each step.
- Auto-fallback: if any gate breaches (configurable), traffic is automatically shifted back to the previous stable variant and the canary is quarantined for postmortem.
- Emergency pin: for critical routes, customers can request a pinned model/version that receives 100% of traffic for a configurable time window; pinning requires product approval and scoped guardrails.

I attached a first-pass SLO/SLA draft and a short telemetry-gate example for your SREs to review. Laura / Aditya — can you confirm whether the commercial team can accept pinning as an operational entitlement (we typically reserve it for enterprise + Dedicated customers unless we define safety constraints)?

Next steps: 1) Aisha reviews attached SLO draft, 2) Product (Rishi) to confirm guardrails and explicit thresholds, 3) Procurement to incorporate language into contract. Happy to jump on a 30 min call if helpful.

On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 11:22 AM aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rishi — could you provide the recommended guardrail matrix (metrics, thresholds, monitoring hooks) and confirm whether pinning requires Dedicated capacity for 99.95+ uptime?

Hi all — thanks for the context. Below is our recommended baseline for an enterprise-grade canary + auto-fallback policy that we can ship as an operational playbook and include in contract language as a mitigant to SLA credits. Note this is a product-approved default; we can adjust thresholds with engineering sign-off.

Recommended Canary & Auto-fallback Guardrails (baseline):
- Canary duration: 30 minutes minimum per step (configurable 10-60m)
- Traffic ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (each step conditioned on telemetry gate pass)
- Telemetry gates evaluated per step:
  - Error rate (5xx or inference exceptions): fail if > 0.3% over step window
  - p99 latency: fail if increases > 2x baseline or exceeds 300ms absolute
  - Request success rate: fail if drops > 0.5% from baseline
- Auto-fallback behavior: immediate traffic revert to previous stable variant on gate failure; canary quarantined and flagged for postmortem
- Emergency pin: allowed for routes marked critical. Pin requests must specify duration (max 72 hours without product escalation) and an owner (customer SRE + Redwood on-call). Pin persists until explicit unpin or expiry.
- Observability: per-request trace id, sampled full traces for failed requests, and token-level cost/latency metrics. Logs retained 90 days by default for enterprise customers.
- Dedicated capacity recommendation: for hard 99.95+ uptime commitments we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to guarantee capacity isolation. Hosted customers can attain similar behavior but are subject to provider capacity constraints and longer lead times for guarantees.

I attached a telemetry-gate-config.yaml with the config schema we propose. Operational items we need from Horizon: baseline metrics (current p95/p99), a list of critical routes you plan to pin, and a designated SRE contact for on-call signoffs.

If Horizon agrees, we can draft contract wording that defines the gating metrics and the exception process (who authorizes pin, how rollback happens, SL adjustments while pin active).

- Rishi Malhotra
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
